chapter_theme: The samadhi of the pranava (பிரணவ சமாதி): Om, gross and subtle, holds within it the one word, form and the formless and all distinctions; the elements, the moving and unmoving and the souls arise from it, and it is the form of both soul and Parasiva. Those on the true path pass beyond its measures and rest at the end of knowing and the known.
structure_note: The gross and higher pranava (2675); what is within Om (2676, 2677); its body and supports (2678); and the teaching and goal of the sanmargis (2679, 2680).

2675.reading: The gross pranava is the great word of the bliss of one's own form; the subtle that sustains it is the woman of the higher form; the seal she bore is its cause there; and the higher pranava is the street of Vedanta.
2675.nuance: தூல (gross), சூக்கும (subtle) and மேலை (higher) pranava are grades of Om in mantra theory. The woman (பெண்) is taken as Shakti and சூலித்த முத்திரை (the seal she conceived) is obscure. The verse ends by placing the highest Om on the road of Vedanta.

2676.reading: Within the omkara called Om is the one word; within it are form and the formless; within it are many distinctions; and the omkara called Om is bright release and attainment.
2676.nuance: ஓம்எனும் ஓங்காரம் opens every line. ஒருமொழி (the one word) may be Om itself as the single source of speech, or the great saying of identity. உருஅரு (form and the formless) is a standard pair for the manifest and unmanifest Lord.

2677.reading: The five elements arose within omkara, the moving and unmoving arose within it, beyond omkara the three kinds of souls came to be, and omkara is the form of both soul and Parasiva.
2677.nuance: உயிர் மூன்று is traditionally the three classes of souls by their malams (vijnanakala, pralayakala, sakala). ஓங்காரா தீதத்து (beyond omkara) sits oddly between lines that place everything within it; it may mean the souls stand at Om's further edge.

2678.reading: The classes of letters become bliss and Brahman, the sun becomes the moving and unmoving in the world, and all the supports reasoned out are his body: so those who gathered and grasped knowledge without lack have known.
2678.nuance: வருக்கம் (class of letters) and அருக்கம் (the sun, or the small) are obscure here, and சுகமாம் may be 'is bliss' or a name. I take the verse as listing what Om becomes; the reading is tentative.

2679.reading: The mountain-like confusions born of the mind, the steady vision that is the way of the lamp, the holy place, lineage and austerity made one's own, and the good: all this is the teaching of the true path.
2679.nuance: மனோபவம் (mind-born) can also be a name of Kama, and மலையும் may be 'mountain' or 'that confuse'. தீப நெறி (the way of the lamp) may be the inner light of meditation. The list is loosely joined, and whether the confusions are to be taught or removed is not said.

2680.reading: For the sanmargis, who speak of the sixteen-fold path, passing beyond the end of the twelve that moves, the end joined in the fourteen, and the bow, they climb and abide at the end of knowledge and the known.
2680.nuance: ஈராறு (twelve) and ஈரேழ் (fourteen) are numbered stages, perhaps kalas of the moon and sun or finger-breadths of breath; கோதண்டம் (the bow) is traditionally the brow region in the yogic body. ஞானஞேயாந்தம் is the end where knowledge and its object no longer differ.

links.note: 2664 says that one who stands in the sixteen-fold path (சோடச மார்க்கம்) sees as other what seemed oneself; 2680 places the same path among the sanmargis and names the stages they pass beyond to rest at the end of knowing.
2677 makes Om the source of elements, world and souls; 2699, on the five letters, takes Om apart as A, U and M and turns from it to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name.

source_issues: 2675 line 2 reads மேலைப் சொரூபப்பெண், a sandhi error, probably for மேலைச் சொரூபப்பெண்.
2678 (வருக்கம், அருக்கம்) and 2679 line 1 are obscure and may be corrupt.
